entries.title: Symbolizer opacity: whole symbol or each part
entries.question: With `opacity: 0.5`, is the symbol made translucent as a whole, or are fill and stroke made translucent separately? Separately, the stroke and fill overlap shows through.

entries.title: Casing beneath or above the stroke
entries.question: A road with a 14 px yellow stroke, a red casing extending 4 px on each side at 60 % opacity (so what lies under it shows through) and a thin white centre line. Is the casing drawn beneath the stroke (an outline) or on top of it?

entries.title: Casing at crossings
entries.question: Two cased roads crossing. Does each road draw its casing together with its own stroke, or are all casings drawn before any stroke, so the crossing merges?

variants.label: Each road with its own casing

entries.title: What casing width means
entries.question: The stroke is 12 px wide and `casing.width` is 3 px. Is 3 px the casing's total width, or how far it extends beyond each side of the stroke?

variants.label: Total width: 3 px, hidden under the stroke

entries.title: Font outline beneath or above the glyphs
entries.question: Text with a 2 px white outline over a dark background. Is the outline drawn beneath the glyphs (a halo) or on top of them?

entries.title: Which zOrder is drawn on top
entries.question: Two overlapping features. Lakes come first in the data but have `zOrder: 2`; Forest has `zOrder: 1`. Is the higher zOrder drawn on top?

entries.title: Hatch angle direction
entries.question: A hatch fill with `angle: 30`. Clockwise or counter-clockwise from horizontal?

entries.title: Units of dashPattern
entries.question: A 6 px wide line with `dashPattern: [4, 2]`. Are the values pixels, or multiples of the stroke width?

entries.title: Default hot spot of an Image
entries.question: A pin icon on a point (black cross = the point's location). Without an explicit `hotSpot`, which part of the image sits on the point?

entries.title: The default marker
entries.question: A style that sets only a fill and a stroke, and no marker. Clause 7's defaults say the default Marker is a single default Dot (white, 10 px), and markers are drawn at points, line vertices and polygon centroids. Does every feature get a white dot?

variants.label: The default Dot, as the table says

entries.title: What a stipple or dot-pattern dot looks like
entries.question: A stipple fill (`ratio: 0.15`, left) and a dot pattern (`distance: 14 px`, right), both with a dark green fill color. Neither the requirements nor the model say how big a dot is or which color it has.

variants.label: Small dots in the fill color (draft renderer's choice)

entries.title: Which label priority wins
entries.question: Two nearby places whose labels overlap. Lillestrøm has `priority: 2`, Strømmen `priority: 8`. Only one label fits. Which one is kept?

entries.title: Units of label minSpacing
entries.question: A road labelled with `minSpacing: 60` at 5 m per pixel. Is 60 in pixels or in metres?

entries.title: Labels on top of everything
entries.question: A labelled harbour point, and a pier polygon drawn after it (higher zOrder). Is the label drawn in a separate pass on top, or with its own feature?

entries.title: Example 5: colorMap between and beyond entries
entries.question: Example 5's color map, stretched from 0–2500 m to Rondane's 500–2000 m (same colors). Between entries, are colors interpolated or stepped? Below 500 m (the valley floors) and above 2000 m (the summits), is the first or last color used, or nothing?

entries.title: Gradient angle convention
entries.question: A linear gradient with `angle: 120`, from navy through red to gold. Where does 0° point, and which way does the angle turn?

entries.title: Gradient position and size: per feature or per map
entries.question: Three parcels with a radial gradient, `position: [0.5, 0.5]`, `size: 1`. Relative to each feature, or to the map?

entries.title: Rules, selectors, nested rules and visibility
entries.question: Each parcel gets the color its rules give it. Farm: silver (only the layer rule applies), with the default black 1 px stroke. Large forest: forest green (nested rule). Small forest (area < 2000): light green (a rule nested twice). Lake: blue with a 3 px navy stroke. The second farm (hidden = true) is not drawn: the dashed outline only shows where it would be. Grey italic labels are annotations, not part of the style.

entries.title: Rules depending on the scale (1:5 000)
entries.question: The dots are shown at both scales; a nested rule on viz.sd < 10 000 adds the labels, so they show at 1:5 000 only.

entries.title: Rules depending on the scale (1:20 000 (the same places, smaller))
entries.question: The dots are shown at both scales; a nested rule on viz.sd < 10 000 adds the labels, so they show at 1:5 000 only.

entries.title: Partial updates (alter) and array element updates (alter: true)
entries.question: First: a later rule with alter: true changes only the width, so the line stays red. Second: the same rule without alter replaces the whole stroke, so the color falls back to the default black. Third and fourth: the dash pattern [16, 8] before and after a later rule sets {index: 1, value: 2}, which changes only the gap, to [16, 2].

entries.title: Partial updates (alter) and array element updates (no alter)
entries.question: First: a later rule with alter: true changes only the width, so the line stays red. Second: the same rule without alter replaces the whole stroke, so the color falls back to the default black. Third and fourth: the dash pattern [16, 8] before and after a later rule sets {index: 1, value: 2}, which changes only the gap, to [16, 2].

entries.title: Property values from expressions
entries.question: Stroke width = lanes × 3 + 1 px: the roads with 1, 2 and 4 lanes are 4, 7 and 13 px wide.

entries.title: Fill and stroke
entries.question: Left: a teal fill at opacity 1 with a 2 px black stroke. Right: the same fill at opacity 0.4 over the grey band, with a 6 px crimson stroke at opacity 0.6.

entries.title: Units of measure
entries.question: At 2 px per metre: 4 px, 2 mm (7.1 px at 0.28 mm per pixel) and 10 m (20 px).

entries.title: Where markers go
entries.question: A dot at the point, at every vertex of the line, and at the centroid of the polygon.

entries.title: Graphic position offset
entries.question: The black cross is the point. A red dot (stroke width 12 px, so 12 px across) is drawn 30 px right of it, and a blue one 20 px above (positive y is up).

entries.title: Text and fonts
entries.question: Three texts at the same point (black cross): serif 16 pt bold, sans-serif 12 pt italic in dark red, monospace 10 pt. Left, centre and right alignment put the cross at the start, middle and end of the text.

entries.title: Image tint and black tint
entries.question: The same black-and-white icon four times. Left: unchanged (the defaults, tint white and blackTint black). Then tint gold (the white parts turn gold), blackTint darkRed (the black parts turn dark red), and both (lightSkyBlue and navy). The grey door is halfway between black and white, so it takes the colour halfway between blackTint and tint.

entries.title: Dash offset
entries.question: Both lines use dashPattern [16, 8]; the lower one has dashOffset 8 px, so its dashes start 8 px later.

entries.title: Hatch width and distance
entries.question: Left: the defaults (1 px lines every 10 px at 45°). Middle: width 3 px. Right: distance 20 px.

entries.title: Font outline size, opacity and color
entries.question: On the dark band: a 1 px white outline, a 4 px yellow outline, and a 4 px white outline at opacity 0.3.

entries.title: Dot pattern distance
entries.question: Left: dots every 8 px both ways. Right: horizontal 20 px, vertical 8 px, so columns of closely spaced dots, 20 px apart.

entries.title: Coverage opacity map
entries.question: Example 5's colors (stretched to Rondane's 500–2000 m) with an opacityMap from 0 at 500 m to 1 at 2000 m, over a striped background: the stripes show through the valleys and disappear under the peaks. Elevation data © Kartverket, CC BY 4.0.

entries.title: Gradient types and keys
entries.question: Linear, radial, repeating and conic, each from white through orange (at 30 %) to dark red, as their keys say. The conic gradient goes once around its centre, so its end (dark red) meets its start (white) in a sharp edge.
